source_name: World Bank Group Country Survey — Kosovo 2025 (microdata catalog 8127)
why_relevant: Stakeholder-opinion survey rather than statistics, but useful for identifying which Kosovo institutions and data themes the WB engages with — an actor-map input for the wider source landscape.

source_name: European Commission — Kosovo Report 2025 (SWD(2025) 752 final), enlargement country report series
why_relevant: Annual accession-linked assessment with dedicated sections on Chapter 4 (free movement of capital / payment systems), Chapter 9 (financial services), Chapter 17/18 (economic and monetary policy, statistics). Carries narrative and often figures on payment services law alignment, SEPA/TIPS progress, interbank payment system (KIPS), statistical capacity — a compulsory, periodic, comparable time series since 2008.

source_name: Raporti për Kosovën 2025 — Albanian translation of the EC country report (EEAS / EU Office in Kosovo)
why_relevant: Official Albanian version of the same report. Gives the authoritative local-language terminology (sistemi i pagesave, shërbimet e pagesave, sektori financiar, paraja e gatshme) that unlocks downstream Albanian-language searching of domestic actors; also the version domestic media and institutions quote.

source_name: Izveštaj o Kosovu 2025 — Serbian translation of the EC country report (EEAS / EU Office in Kosovo)
why_relevant: Serbian-language version of the annual EC assessment; source of Serbian terminology (platni promet, platne usluge, finansijski sektor, gotovina) and the version circulated among Kosovo-Serb institutions and Belgrade-facing media. Older editions confirm a stable URL/file pattern back to at least 2023.

source_name: European Commission DG ECFIN — Economic Reform Programme (ERP) assessments, Kosovo chapter
source_subtype: economic governance assessment / institutional paper series
why_relevant: Annual EU assessment of Kosovo's medium-term macro-fiscal and structural reform programme; the standing channel where financial-sector deepening, informality/cash economy, financial inclusion and payment-market reforms are scored and turned into Joint Conclusions. Provides quantified macro tables useful as denominators for payment/card penetration metrics.

source_name: Eurostat — Enlargement / international cooperation statistics portal (candidate & potential-candidate data, incl. Kosovo)
why_relevant: The EU's harmonised statistical entry point for Kosovo: enlargement-country datasets, 'Enlargement countries — statistical overview' Statistics Explained articles, and 'Key figures on enlargement countries'. Supplies EU-comparable macro/monetary/ICT and household indicators that frame card, POS and cash-usage analysis.

source_name: Eurostat — 'Basic figures on the candidate countries and potential candidates' factsheet series
why_relevant: Compact recurring factsheet giving Kosovo's headline indicators on an EU-comparable basis; fastest reference layer for population, GDP, household and digital-uptake denominators used in per-capita payment metrics.

source_name: Eurostat — Peer Review of the Kosovo statistical system against the European Statistics Code of Practice (+ improvement actions)
why_relevant: Assesses the reliability and production capacity of Kosovo official statistics — decisive for judging how much weight to put on any Kosovo-origin market/payment statistic. The 2017 peer-review report and the published improvement-action plan are directly downloadable.

source_name: Eurostat — Enlargement policy and statistical cooperation (Statistics Explained) / IPA statistical cooperation programming
why_relevant: Pointer page mapping which EU instruments (IPA multi-beneficiary statistical programmes, global assessments, peer reviews) fund and evaluate Kosovo statistics, and which domestic bodies are counterparts. Snowballs into KAS/CBK statistical-capacity actors and into the specific IPA project documentation.

source_name: European Payments Council — SEPA schemes' geographical scope list (EPC409-09) and country inclusion decisions
why_relevant: The authoritative European register of which jurisdictions are inside SEPA scheme scope. Kosovo's accession status here is the single hardest fact governing euro-payment integration for a unilaterally euroised economy; the versioned list (v7.0 May 2025 → v8.0 Dec 2025) gives a clean change-detection target, and EPC news items announce each Western Balkans inclusion.

source_name: European Commission (DG NEAR) news — SEPA inclusion statements for Western Balkans partners
why_relevant: Commission communications that document the political/legal conditionality behind SEPA inclusion in the region — the template Kosovo must satisfy (payment services law alignment, AML framework, PSP supervision). Useful as an early-warning feed for a Kosovo announcement.

source_name: European Commission — Growth Plan for the Western Balkans / Reform and Growth Facility, Kosovo Reform Agenda and payment-condition tracking
why_relevant: Kosovo's Reform Agenda (approved Oct 2024) turns reform steps — including digital transition and business-environment measures that touch payment infrastructure and formalisation of the cash economy — into disbursement conditions with dated milestones and a public tracking dashboard. Gives forward-looking, dated commitments rather than retrospective description.

source_name: EEAS — EU Office in Kosovo / EUSR: SAA Sub-committee on Economic and Financial Issues and Statistics conclusions
why_relevant: Treaty-based bilateral body (SAA) that meets roughly annually and whose published conclusions record the EU's specific statistical and financial-sector asks of Kosovo — including statistics production and financial-sector supervision. Conclusions are also posted by the Ministry of European Integration, giving a local-language mirror.

source_name: EEAS — EU Office in Kosovo / EUSR main delegation site (multilingual en/sq/sr document hub)
why_relevant: The distribution hub for every EU document about Kosovo in all three working languages, including report translations, sub-committee conclusions, project announcements and EU-funded financial-sector/digitalisation initiatives. Primary snowball node for this cell.

source_name: European Parliament — annual resolution and AFET report on the Commission reports on Kosovo
why_relevant: Parliamentary scrutiny layer that restates and sometimes sharpens Commission findings on Kosovo's economy, informality and EU financial integration; useful for detecting which financial-sector issues are politically salient and for citations to underlying data.

source_name: Council of Europe — PECK II project: Assessment report on Kosovo's compliance with international AML/CFT standards (FATF/MONEYVAL methodology)
why_relevant: The functional substitute for a MONEYVAL mutual evaluation, since Kosovo is not a Council of Europe member and therefore not a MONEYVAL member. Applies FATF/MONEYVAL methodology and is the main European assessment discussing Kosovo's cash-intensive economy, cash-transaction thresholds, non-bank money transfer and AML controls on cash.

source_name: Council of Europe — MONEYVAL / Economic Crime and Cooperation Division (regional comparators and any future Kosovo engagement)
why_relevant: Even without Kosovo as a member, MONEYVAL's 5th-round reports for Albania, North Macedonia, Serbia, Montenegro and Bosnia give directly comparable European measurements of cash intensity, cash-courier and cash-threshold regimes in the same market region — the best available benchmark set. Also the place any future Kosovo engagement would be announced.

source_name: ECB — publications on official euroisation/dollarisation and the international role of the euro (ECB Occasional Paper No. 11 and successors)
why_relevant: The ECB's institutional position on unilateral euroisation — the framing that determines why Kosovo gets no euro-area cash-issuance data, no direct ECB payment statistics coverage, and no Eurosystem cash-cycle reporting. Essential for correctly caveating any euro-cash-in-Kosovo estimate.

source_name: ECB — SPACE study, euro-area payments statistics and euro banknote circulation data (as comparator / euro-outside-euro-area context)
why_relevant: ECB's payment statistics and the SPACE consumer payment-attitudes study are the reference measurement of card/cash/POS behaviour in the euro area. Kosovo is excluded from the reporting population, but these give the methodological template and the benchmark values against which any Kosovo card/POS/cash indicator must be read. ECB estimates of euro banknotes circulating outside the euro area are the only European-level handle on euro cash held in places like Kosovo.

source_name: EBRD — Transition Report country assessments: Kosovo
why_relevant: European multilateral bank producing an annual Kosovo assessment that has explicitly covered the CBK National Retail Payments Strategy 2021-26, cashless-payments-per-capita and account-ownership objectives, and Kosovo's cash-transaction restrictions. One of the few European institutional sources with concrete retail-payment policy detail on Kosovo.

source_name: German Economic Team — analysis of Kosovo's SEPA accession process (EU-adjacent advisory, non-official)
why_relevant: One of the few dedicated analyses of the two-step Kosovo SEPA accession mechanism (country inclusion in geographical scope, then PSP scheme adherence) and the legislative prerequisites for the Ministry of Finance and CBK. Useful as a pointer to the underlying EPC/EC criteria; not an official source and should be corroborated.

source_name: e-Prokurimi — Kosovo national e-procurement platform (KRPP/PPRC)
why_relevant: Single mandatory portal where every Kosovo contracting authority publishes contract notices (B05 'Njoftim per Kontrate'), award notices (B08 'Njoftim per dhenie te kontrates') and signed-contract notices (B52). Tender dossiers and technical specifications state quantities of ATMs, POS terminals, card personalisation volumes and switch capacity that no CBK/statistical publication reports. Document pages are directly addressable, e.g. .../SPIN_PROD/application/ipn/DocumentManagement/DokumentPodaciFrm.aspx?id=3489060.

source_name: KRPP / PPRC OCDS API — Open Contracting data for Kosovo procurement
why_relevant: Machine-readable Open Contracting Data Standard feed of the whole e-Prokurimi corpus: tender titles, buyers, suppliers, values, procedure type, lots, awards. Coverage reported March 2016 - March 2026 with bulk JSONL.gz / XLSX / CSV downloads (all-time JSON ~23 MB). This is the highest-leverage single endpoint for systematically finding every ATM/POS/payment-system contract in Kosovo over a decade.

source_name: KRPP — Komisioni Rregullativ i Prokurimit Publik (Public Procurement Regulatory Commission)
why_relevant: Regulator and operator of the notice regime; publishes annual public-procurement reports (aggregate contract values by sector/CPV), the notice-form standards (B05/B08/B52) needed to parse dossiers, legislation, and an archive. Essential for interpreting and normalising the tender corpus.

source_name: Prokurimi Hapur / Otvorena nabavka — Open Procurement Kosovo
why_relevant: Civil-society re-publication and analytics layer over Kosovo procurement data, available in Albanian, Serbian (sr-Latn) and English. Usually far easier to search and filter by buyer/supplier than the government portal, and preserves records that rotate off e-Prokurimi. Useful for identifying which vendors repeatedly win ATM/POS/payment-system lots.

source_name: OSHP — Organi Shqyrtues i Prokurimit (Procurement Review Body) decisions & complaint database
why_relevant: Complaint decisions quote tender technical specifications, bid prices, unit counts and evaluation detail that are often redacted or absent from the published notice. Searchable by contracting authority, economic operator, tender category and value — an excellent way to reconstruct disputed ATM/POS/card-system procurements and the competing vendors.

source_name: Demokracia Plus — OSHP decisions database (oshp.dplus.org)
why_relevant: NGO-built, full-text searchable mirror of Procurement Review Body decisions — typically more scrape-friendly than the official OSHP application and retains older decisions. Good fallback pointer into disputed payment-infrastructure tenders.
